transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because my talking has been kind of… messy lately. I don’t mean to make a big deal out of it, but I can’t really keep my words in a straight line anymore.

Like I’ll start telling someone about an overnight shift, and then somehow I’m talking about soccer, or paint colors, or patient charts, and I can tell people are getting lost. I’m trying to answer normally, it just… doesn’t come out that way. Is that okay to say?
Lately, have you been feeling unusually high or euphoric?

Um… unusually high? I don’t think so. Not like, happy in a weird way or on top of the world or anything.

I mean, I have little moments where I try to act okay, especially around people, but I wouldn’t call it euphoric. If that’s what you mean.
Have you been feeling like you have way more energy than usual lately?

I don’t think so… not way more, no. I’ve been getting through things, I guess, but I wouldn’t say I’m energized or anything like that.

I’m sorry, is that the kind of thing you mean? Like feeling wired? Because I haven’t really noticed that.
Have you been feeling like people are trying to harm you or plot against you?

I don’t want to sound dramatic… but yeah, kind of.

I keep thinking the supervisors are changing my shifts on purpose, and watching me on the unit cameras to see if I’m unsafe or something. People say it’s just staffing shortages, and I try to believe that, but it doesn’t feel like that to me.

I know that probably sounds bad. I’m not trying to accuse anyone, I just… that’s how it feels.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?

No… I mean, I don’t think so.

Sometimes I’ll think I heard something, like a noise or someone talking nearby, but when I check there’s usually some explanation, or I’m just tired. I wouldn’t say I’m hearing voices when no one’s around. Is that… is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
Have you found yourself feeling emotionally flat, like your face or voice doesn’t show much feeling even when something matters to you?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think so… or at least I haven’t noticed it.

People haven’t said I look blank or anything. I mean, I can be quiet, especially when I’m tired or stressed, but I wouldn’t say I don’t feel things. Maybe I don’t always show it right? I’m not sure if that’s what you mean.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day lately?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days I wake up already feeling really heavy, like empty inside.

And after work sometimes I’ll just sit in my car for a while and… cry before I can even drive home. I know that probably sounds like a lot. But yeah, it’s been most days.
Have you been acting in ways that feel very disorganized or that other people have said seem unusual or hard to understand?

Um… maybe a little. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m doing anything really bizarre, because I can usually do my job, but there have been moments at work where I sort of… get stuck.

Like I’ve caught myself rocking in the hallway, or copying a patient’s tapping without really meaning to. And once or twice I’ll be standing there with my gloves only halfway on, just kind of frozen, even though I know I’m supposed to be doing rounds.

I know that probably doesn’t sound good. I’m not trying to be difficult or anything… it just happens sometimes, I guess.
Have there been times when you still felt watched or suspicious even when you were not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think there was a time like that.

I wasn’t, like, in the really deep depressed place for a few weeks, or at least not as bad. But I still felt like the cameras at work were watching me more than they should be, and like the supervisors were kind of monitoring what I was doing.

I tried to just act normal, because I know that sounds… paranoid or something. But I was definitely more guarded at work. I’d be careful where I stood and what I said, even when my mood wasn’t that low. Does that make sense?
Have these problems with suspiciousness and your speech being hard to keep on track been going on for more than one month?

Yeah… it’s been more than a month. I guess I was hoping it was just a phase or stress or something, but if I’m being honest, the feeling watched stuff and getting kind of mixed up or stuck has been going on for… about a year. Maybe a year and a month.

I don’t mean it’s been every single second, but it’s been around that long, yeah.
Was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you still felt watched or suspicious even though you were not depressed at all?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I wasn’t in that really deep depressed place for a few weeks, so I guess that would count.

But I still had the feeling that the cameras at work were kind of focused on me, and that supervisors were watching or tracking what I was doing. I tried not to make a big deal out of it, and I kept telling myself to just act normal, but I was still guarded there.

I know that probably sounds bad… but yes, there was a stretch like that.
Have you lost motivation to do everyday things, even basic tasks, more than you used to?

Yeah… I guess I have, more than I want to admit.

I used to do stuff without really thinking about it—like sketching mural ideas, cooking for friends, playing soccer on weekends. That used to feel like me, you know? Lately it just feels kind of… pointless, or like too much effort.

I don’t want to sound lazy. I still try to do what I have to, but most days I end up ignoring messages and just staying in my apartment. I know that’s probably not great.
During those depressed periods, did you feel worthless nearly every day?

I… I’m not totally sure how to answer that.

I felt pretty low about myself, yeah, and like I wasn’t doing enough or being the person I should be. But “worthless” nearly every day feels… I don’t know, it feels like a strong word. Maybe sometimes it got close to that, but I don’t want to say it wrong or make it sound worse than it was.
Was there ever a time when the suspiciousness and your speech problems lasted for at least a month while you were not depressed?

I’m not sure I can honestly say a full month, or that the speech thing was there the whole time.

There was definitely a stretch of a few weeks where I wasn’t in that really deep depressed place, but I still thought the cameras at work were kind of on me, and that supervisors were monitoring what I was doing. I kept acting guarded, trying to seem normal.

But I don’t want to say “at least a month” if I’m not sure.
Was there ever a full month when your speech was still getting mixed up like this even though you were not depressed?

I think… yeah, I mean, that’s kind of what brings me in, honestly. I don’t know if I tracked it perfectly as a “full month,” but my words have been getting mixed up even when I’m not feeling really depressed.

Like I’ll start telling someone about an overnight shift, and then somehow I’m talking about soccer, paint colors, patient charts… and I can see people’s faces like they’re trying to follow me but they’re lost. I try to pull it back and make it sound normal, but it doesn’t always come out in a straight line. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have other people told you that your behavior seems very odd or hard to make sense of?

Yeah… a couple people have kind of said I seemed “off,” or asked if I was okay.

I don’t think I’m, like, trying to act strange or anything. But at work I’ve caught myself doing things that probably look weird… like rocking in the hallway, or copying a patient’s tapping without really meaning to. One time I was just standing there with my gloves half on, like I was stuck, even though I knew I was supposed to be doing rounds.

I know that sounds bad. I’m not trying to be difficult or unsafe or anything. It’s just… sometimes I realize after a second that I must look hard to understand. Is that what you mean?
Over the whole time these symptoms have been going on, have you been depressed for most of that time?

Yeah… I think if I’m being honest, probably yes.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but looking back, that heavy empty feeling and not really caring about things has been there for most of this whole stretch. Even when the worries about cameras were quieter, or when I wasn’t talking as scattered, I still didn’t feel like myself.

So… yes, I think depressed for most of it is fair to say. Is that the kind of timeline you’re asking about?

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms have been present for >1 year, with at least 2 weeks of delusional suspiciousness outside depressive episodes, while depressive symptoms were present for most of the total illness duration. This rules against F20.0 and F20.1 and supports schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.

Crucially, psychotic symptoms were present for at least 2 weeks outside a major depressive episode, supporting schizoaffective disorder rather than a mood disorder with psychotic features.
